*Micchattaniyatattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.39) is a canonical Abhidhamma text located within the *Paṭṭhāna* division of the Pali Tipiṭaka. Structurally, it treats the intersection of the triad on states with fixed destiny or wrongness (*micchattaniyatattika*) with the dyad of root conditions (*hetuduka*) within the conditional relations framework.

No external cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit are documented for this section [DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis shows extensive internal formulaic overlap across the *Paṭṭhāna*, with 61 matching passages shared across 23 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most prominent alignments occur with other dyad-triad permutations, including *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25), *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1), *Sekkhattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.35), *Cūḷantaraduka, Hetuduka* (Patthana 18.14), *Parittārammaṇattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.37), and another text sharing the same triad, *Micchattaniyatattika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 23.33) [DharmaNexus].
